C023.notes: SER EU-DE-001. Large 20 in oak wreath · 1918. Iron wartime type — copper/nickel diverted for the war. Year the Empire ended. Not FRG brass Pfennig — different chapter. New oldest in the vault (was 1939). Common date; value is history + base-metal survivor, not hype.
C023.story: A 1918 20-heller coin from Austria, struck in iron during the First World War under Emperor Charles I, when copper and nickel went to the war. The side shown has a large 20 in an oak wreath with the date 1918 below and no lettering; the other side shows the crowned double-headed eagle with the Austrian shield. Stefan Schwartz engraved it.

C272.label: Austria · 1925 · 2 Groschen
C272.notes: Phase 1 by Grok from both sides of the owner chat photos (2026-10-01). Austria was added to the issuer list with this coin.
C272.story: An Austrian 2 groschen from 1925. One side is the federal cross with the date, the other a large 2 over the word GROSCHEN. 1925 is the year Austria introduced the schilling, and the groschen was its small change.
